I really wanted this, and I'm very glad I picked it up. This has a lot going for it, and hopefully it'll be interesting to those of you who are also looking into one:

The Packaging

The packaging is plain. Mine came in a plastic bag inside a yellow lacy drawstring kind of thing. Plenty of spare screws and the like, as well as a hex key for the little screws in the deck. There are some spare O-rings as well, just to be safe. All in, nothing too special packaging wise.

The Looks

This guy is short. Super short. It's 35mm tall, the same height as two 18650s wide, and it somehow fits 5m: inside of there. I don't get it. Special Hungarian space magic, because I have a few gennies with 5mL tanks, and they are way taller than this one.

I got the brushed stainless steel version, rather than the polished, and it's really quite handsome. The heat sink fins are super sweet, although not quite as effective as I'd like them to be (more on that in the performance section later on). They make this little conical shape that's a nice touch and something that igetcha69 mentions in his video reviews.

The AFC ring to choose the airflow is nice. It doesn't have too much of a seam from the top cap that screws on, nor the body of the top cap and it has strong fit and finish.

On the bottom, there is some logoing/laser engraving/serialization, but I almost never look down there (and you'll find out in the performance section especially why), and it is what it is.

Overall, I think it's quite charming, and the small size is very nice for those of us looking for something more on the compact side.

The Deck

I decided to do a special section for this particular RBA because the deck is absolutely nuts. It's entirely modular, and you can configure it however you want.

First, the positive post has two knurled nuts on it, one of them secures the post to the RBA, and the other is a capture. There is a hole in the positive post that the top knurled nut closes down over to capture your positive lead(s).

There are 4 wick holes in this deck. Two 3mm holes and two 4.5mm holes. The 3mm holes are supposed to be for mesh/cable, and the 4.5mm holes are for cotton/silica/ekowool/what have you.

To choose your holes, there are two different deck caps. One of them leaves 2 wick holes open, and the other leaves just 1 for your preference. Unfortunately, I haven't checked to see if you can mix-and-match diameters, although I'm not sure why you would necessarily want to do that. Each deck cap is also a chamber reducer, and these things absolutely work - more on those below in the Performance section.

When you have selected your number of wick holes, you also have a fill port that has a threaded bung. The fill port is generously sized to accept droppers, low-gauge luer-lock syringes, needle tip bottles, my UCan, and plastic tipped bottles. I haven't found anything I can't use to fill it yet.

The posts and deck caps are held in place with some tiny hex screws, fortunately it comes with a tool to adjust them, but I've been using a metric hex variety tool just fine.

The Performance

Note: so far all of my builds have been dual coils, I'll be describing my experiences with two of my most successful ones.

I decided to do things a little bit differently initially with this RBA. I decided to do a single strand style build, but using the negative post as the "core" (in a dripper you'd generally use the positive post as the "core"). I think it's certainly helped with the classic genny short issues, although with the fenagling you have to do , it's hard to make it come out pretty. Contact coils on both sides, 3mm inner diameter with 26AWG coming out to ~0.8 ohms.

Inside of the coils, I did solid wicks of #400 SS mesh 3mm wide (oxidized, of course). It can take a little twisting to get everything snug inside, but it all came out great.

I didn't have much break-in time with my wicks, maybe a tank full of liquid to get where I needed to be. After that I was in absolute flavor heaven. On any of the airflow settings, I am just blown away. The temperature varies. Stainless mesh is such a fantastic heat sink that I cranked my wattage up to 25W just to get things rolling, and it stays hot hot hot. The whole atty gets hot-hot-hot, no matter if you leave it on the widest airflow setting (2 x 2.5mm holes, allowing for some tasty lung hits).

Even with my wick holes completely filled up, I never had any wicking issues. No under or over wicking - the juice I used has flowed just fine (mostly Azeroth from Coval). I really haven't had any leaking problems to speak of, but the longest it was on its side was about a half hour.

My other build was 2.5mm 7x19 SS cable. The cable expands when getting oxidized, so I had to use the 4.5mm wick holes. This overwicks. So much. This leaves a lot of room for playing with some Pinoy builds (SS cable leading up to standard dripper builds), but I haven't quite gotten around to that.

Overall, the performance is incredible. Even with my exceptionally high-wicking SS cable builds, I really can't find anything that beats the flavor. The fact that you can set the airflow to whatever you please (it has roughly a zillion settings) without impacting wicking is something I've always loved about Genesis styles.

The deck caps reducing the chamber in conjunction with the dome inside the top cap means you are getting impeccable flavor every single time you take a drag. The only reason this needs the genny tilt is to make sure you're getting the last few drops out of the tank.

Overall

The only possible negative is that despite the fact that this tank is so expensive, it still has a PMMA tank section, so that means no tank crackers. I've found a stainless steel replacement one on VapeRev, and it's about $20, so that will address most everyone's issue with that.

The airflow is adjustable from incredibly tight all the way to wide open (1.2mm - 2 x 2.5mm), giving you either those super flavorful or incredibly airy lung hits.

The flavor and vapor coming from this are both phenomenal. I haven't had issues with it on my ZNA, SVD 2.0 or MVP 3.0. Everything makes this work, and it will work for you. Genesis style builds are definitely more effort up-front, but there is absolutely no reason not to purchase this if you have the funds.

Furthermore, this is a member of a growing family that I started talking about with the Squape R. This is another atomizer that allows you to use whatever wicking material you please. The Rose V2 also does this. I think for the sheer utility of that, these kinds of atomizers are worth the price tag. It's staggering the amount of customization these allow for with all the variety available to them. I sincerely could not recommend this atomizer more, no matter your style. Out of the three, this one allows for the most amount of customization (largely due to the fact that the airflow can vary so widely).

My final verdict on this guy is a sincere 9.6/10, with just a hair few points taken off for the PMMA tank and hex keys.
